title: Windsurf Operating Card
summary: Use Windsurf Cascade with scoped Code and Chat modes, durable rules, reviewed tools, and named checkpoint recovery.
prerequisites: An approved account and model policy

sections.title: Choose Chat or Code based on required authority
paragraphs: Cascade provides conversational and coding modes, tool calls, plans, todo lists, terminal awareness, and checkpoints. Use Chat when explanation or investigation is sufficient and Code only when edits or commands are authorized.
Generated Memories are local context; use versioned workspace Rules or AGENTS.md for durable team guidance that reviewers can inspect.

sections.title: Make plans, rules, and checkpoints reviewable
paragraphs: State the goal, allowed files, tool boundary, and tests before implementation. Review plans, queued messages, terminal actions, and the complete diff rather than accepting a successful-looking summary.
Create named checkpoints around risky experiments and keep Git as the authoritative delivery record. Scope ignore files and repository rules according to data classification.

code.label: Windsurf task card
code.code:
Task: [one observable result]
Scope: [workspace and paths]
Permissions: [Chat/Code, terminal, edit, tools, and network]
Rules: [AGENTS.md and workspace rules]
Checkpoint: [named recovery point]
Verification: [plan, diff, tests, and runtime result]
Recovery: [revert checkpoint, restore Git, reconcile side effects]

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: Expected evidence includes the active rules, selected mode, reviewed plan and tool calls, named checkpoint, Git diff, and exact check output. Verify that local Memories did not become unreviewed project policy.
If Cascade loses context or crosses scope, stop queued work, preserve the trace, restore the named checkpoint or Git state, and retry with explicit durable rules and a smaller task.
